cadence.citation: docs/alarm-lane-design-20260922.md section 2.3; the confirmation rule is T8a 5.5
derivation: the confirmation rule needs 2 consecutive element sets, so a confirmable change becomes visible about 1.513 d after it happens (2 x 0.756 d)
re-reading more often than one median spacing re-reads unchanged element sets, so the work floor is 0.756 d
against a median causal lead of 36.1 d, one work floor of latency is 2.1% of the warning budget
the host timer's own period of 2.0 h is 0.2% of the same budget and buys nothing, because the element sets it would re-read have not changed
so: fire on the host timer, and do work only when the object's newest element-set epoch has advanced

inputs.medianEpochSpacingSource: measured over all 1652 watched objects' element sets

leak.sentence: The GEO catalogues remain uncontrolled. This trigger fires 3,812 times inside 517,391 days of provably uncontrolled motion -- 0.288 [0.279, 0.298] of the rate it fires on objects that can manoeuvre, against a bar of 0.10. A rung precision measured here is a property of this detector on this catalogue, not a rate at which objects of a class do anything.

controlB.subsetNote: the committed ledger is a SUBSET -- 10326 rows of 3914621 -- so the joined population is a sample of the ladder's episodes and every row prints its own n. GEO.verdictBasis: S2 Wilson lower bound 0.00374 exceeds S1's point precision 0.00253 on n = 3254
GEO.windowRule: the decade with the most confirmed drift changes (71,661 of 226,422 flag chains), chosen on alert volume, which is outcome-blind

cadence.citation: docs/alarm-lane-design-20260922.md section 2.3; the confirmation rule is T8a 5.5
derivation: the confirmation rule needs 2 consecutive element sets, so a confirmable change becomes visible about 0.987 d after it happens (2 x 0.493 d)
re-reading more often than one median spacing re-reads unchanged element sets, so the work floor is 0.493 d
against a median causal lead of 195.9 d, one work floor of latency is 0.3% of the warning budget
the host timer's own period of 2.0 h is 0.0% of the same budget and buys nothing, because the element sets it would re-read have not changed
so: fire on the host timer, and do work only when the object's newest element-set epoch has advanced

LEO.verdictBasis: every powered rung above S1 has a Wilson lower bound at or below S1's point precision
LEO.windowRule: the earliest span of the decade that holds the largest payload population in this regime for which EVERY alert's 1,095-day horizon still closes inside the archive. Chosen on population and on archive extent, both outcome-blind, and fixed before any figure in this replay existed.

caveats: Mean longitude is a slot coordinate, not a miss distance. Two objects sharing a mean longitude are routinely tens of kilometres apart, kept so by eccentricity- and inclination-vector separation this track does not model. This lane is not a conjunction warning and does not replace one.

The catalogue is a lower bound, never a census. A transfer executed below 0.010 deg/day is invisible, and 33% of the catalogued events had no visible initiating change. Absence of an alert is not evidence of absence of an approach.

horizons.note: the set's horizon is the one the forward-error measurement leaves resolvable; the outcome horizon is the lane's own, so a rung precision can be compared with the single-burn figure it has to beat

inSampleNote: The frozen partition was fitted on the whole 1959-2026 primary arm, which contains this window, so every precision measured here is IN SAMPLE for the taxonomy.
